input.quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
input.rationale: Vendor (Kubient) gives express, affirmative warranties at §9(b) that cover every material term of the preferred position: performance of the Service "in all material respects to industry standards" (p0034), services that "comply with the terms of this Agreement and shall be free from errors that materially affect their utility" (p0038), a no-malicious-code warranty (p0036, viruses/Trojan Horses/worms/back doors), and compliance with all applicable Laws "now and throughout the Term" (p0041). Critically, these warranties are not time-limited to 12 months/90 days — they run for the whole Term, which exceeds the preferred duration. The §13 disclaimer (p0062) does not swallow them: it applies only "Except as expressly set forth herein" and expressly excepts "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so this is not the "AS IS with all warranties disclaimed" walk-away scenario. On remedy, the Agreement contains no repair/replace/refund remedy sentence and no exclusive-remedy or sole-remedy language anywhere; we therefore retain all remedies at law plus the 30-day cure/termination right for material breach in §4(b) (p0016), which is broader than the capped "at Vendor's option" remedy in our model language. Adding that sentence would narrow our position, so we note the absent remedy mechanic in the rationale rather than redlining it. Also noted as minor sub-elements only: the warranty is framed as "industry standards" and freedom from material errors rather than express conformance to documentation, and there is no separate "professional and workmanlike" formulation. No redline proposed.
